标题: New York City High - Rise Building Partially Collapses Due To Gas Explosion
正文(前2500字): A high-rise building in the Bronx partially collapsed on Wednesday (October 1) morning, sending emergency crews into action. The Fire Department of New York (FDNY) reported the incident on Alexander Avenue in the Mott Haven area, where a gas explosion and incinerator shaft collapse occurred at the Mitchel Houses complex. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported so far. About 40 apartments have been evacuated as a precaution. Witnesses described hearing a "loud boom" before seeing part of the building's wall peel away. "The fact that half of the building is gone and you felt it...luckily everybody was able to get out safe, but feeling it and the intensity, and going downstairs, you could barely go downstairs, everybody is trying to go downstairs. People were carrying babies, people got no shoes on, got no coats, no hats, it's cold outside," a resident told WABC. The FDNY, along with the New York Police Department and other emergency services, are conducting search-and-rescue operations. The city's Emergency Management department has confirmed that Con Edison has shut off gas to the affected building, and a temporary shelter has been set up at a nearby community center. New York City Mayor Eric Adams is monitoring the situation and advised residents to avoid the area for their safety. The city's Department of Buildings is on-site to assess the structural integrity of the remaining structure. Video recorded by a resident in a nearby building captured the moment part of the building collapsed, sending debris raining down the side.

正文(前2500字): Hong Kong is mourning the 128 people known to have died in a massive fire at a high-rise apartment complex, a toll that is likely to rise with 150 still missing days after the disaster. Rescue operations at the site in the district of Tai Po, near the border with mainland China, concluded on Friday, though police say they might find more bodies as they comb through the hazardous, burnt-out buildings in coming weeks. Police revised down the number of people unaccounted for to 150 from 200 on Saturday, after confirming with some relatives that they had managed to reconnect with loved ones they initially reported as missing. Hundreds of officers deployed to search for remains found no further bodies but rescued three cats and a turtle, police officials told a press conference. The fire started on Wednesday afternoon and rapidly engulfed seven of the eight 32-storey blocks at the complex, which were wrapped in bamboo scaffolding and green mesh and layered with foam insulation for the renovations. Mainland China on Saturday ordered a nationwide investigation of fire risks at high-rise buildings, especially residential blocks undergoing renovation. Authorities have said the fire alarms at the Wang Fuk Court estate, home to more than 4600 people, had not been working properly. Hong Kong leader John Lee, other officials and civil servants, all dressed in black, stood in silence for three minutes early on Saturday outside the central government offices, where flags were lowered to half-staff. 标题: Pullman arson suspect rescinds insanity plea
正文(前2500字): The man accused of causing last month’s Pullman apartment complex blaze is no longer pleading not guilty by reason of insanity. Elijah Reagan, 40, changed his pleas to not guilty during a second arraignment held Friday morning in Colfax’s Whitman County Superior Court. Reagan faces life in prison if he is convicted of felony first-degree arson. Additionally, he is charged with eluding and malicious damage to property with an explosive device. There was no reason given by Reagen or his attorney Steve Martonick as to why he withdrew his insanity pleas. Authorities believe Reagan set his apartment building on fire with fireworks shot out of a mortar Oct. 5, court documents say. The blaze damaged all 18 units of the complex located on the 100 block of NW Larry Street. All residents were displaced when the structure was deemed “dangerous and unsafe to occupy” by Pullman Fire Department inspectors as a result of the blaze. Reagan allegedly fled the scene after the fire started and led authorities on a car chase down U.S. Highway 195. Court documents show the pursuit ended when Reagen’s tires were spiked at the Lewiston Hill south of Uniontown. Reagan was reportedly in an armed standoff with authorities and the Whitman County SWAT Team, the court documents say. No one was injured during the incident. Court documents show Reagan surrendered several hours after the pursuit began. Officers believe Reagan had been under the influence of methamphetamine that evening. Reagan allegedly admitted to bombing his apartment in a call to his estranged wife, according to the court documents. She told officers Reagan uses methamphetamine. Reagan remains in the Whitman County Jail on $250,000 bail, or $25,000 surety. He is scheduled to appear in court for a jury trial in January. Pearce can be reached at epearce@dnews.com.

Further investigation revealed that Sarita was acting on the directions of Niranjan, 33, and his brother Rajkumar, 27, both residents of Navjeevan Camp. The three allegedly conspired to orchestrate the arson to settle a personal grudge, police added. 标题: Küchenbrand sorgt in Reutlingen für Feuerwehreinsatz - Reutlingen - Reutlinger G
正文(前2500字): REUTLINGEN. Am frühen Sonntagmorgen ist die Feuerwehr zu einem Küchenbrand in einem Mehrfamilienhaus in der Heilbronner Straße ausgerückt. Gegen 2:10 Uhr ging der Notruf bei der Integrierten Leitstelle für Feuerwehr und Rettungsdienst ein. Beim Eintreffen der Feuerwehr drang bereits Rauch aus der betroffenen Wohnung. Unter Atemschutz kämpften sich Einsatzkräfte in die verqualmten Räume vor und brachten die Flammen rasch unter Kontrolle und verhinderten so eine mögliche Ausbreitung des Feuers. Um auszuschließen, dass sich Rauch auch in angrenzende Wohnungen ausgebreitet hatte, kontrollierten weitere Einsatzkräfte das Gebäude. Eine Wohnungstür musste dabei mit Spezialwerkzeug geöffnet werden. Für die übrigen Bewohner bestand keine Gefahr. Die Feuerwehr belüftete die verrauchten Bereiche maschinell. Mit einer Wärmebildkamera wurde die Brandstelle sorgfältig auf mögliche Glutnester überprüft, dazu mussten Teile der Küche demontiert werden. Der Einsatz dauerte rund eine Stunde. Mit insgesamt fünf Fahrzeugen und 20 Einsatzkräften waren die Berufsfeuerwehr und die Abteilung Stadtmitte vor Ort. Polizei und Rettungsdienst unterstützten die Maßnahmen. (pm)

标题: New York City High - Rise Building Partially Collapses Due To Gas Explosion
正文(前2500字): A high-rise building in the Bronx partially collapsed on Wednesday (October 1) morning, sending emergency crews into action. The Fire Department of New York (FDNY) reported the incident on Alexander Avenue in the Mott Haven area, where a gas explosion and incinerator shaft collapse occurred at the Mitchel Houses complex. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported so far. About 40 apartments have been evacuated as a precaution. Witnesses described hearing a "loud boom" before seeing part of the building's wall peel away. "The fact that half of the building is gone and you felt it...luckily everybody was able to get out safe, but feeling it and the intensity, and going downstairs, you could barely go downstairs, everybody is trying to go downstairs. People were carrying babies, people got no shoes on, got no coats, no hats, it's cold outside," a resident told WABC. The FDNY, along with the New York Police Department and other emergency services, are conducting search-and-rescue operations. The city's Emergency Management department has confirmed that Con Edison has shut off gas to the affected building, and a temporary shelter has been set up at a nearby community center. New York City Mayor Eric Adams is monitoring the situation and advised residents to avoid the area for their safety. The city's Department of Buildings is on-site to assess the structural integrity of the remaining structure. Video recorded by a resident in a nearby building captured the moment part of the building collapsed, sending debris raining down the side.

标题: One hospitalized after fire in a 3 - story KC apartment building
正文(前2500字): KANSAS CITY—Authorities are investigating the cause of an apartment fire in Kansas City. Just before 2:30a.m. Wednesday, Kansas City Fire companies were dispatched to a reported apartment fire in the 3400 block of Holmes Road, according to Battalion Chief Riley Nolan. The first arriving company reported nothing showing from the exterior of a 3-story apartment building and entered to investigate. Smoke was encountered on the 3rd floor and crews forced entry into a unit where they found the source and extinguished a small fire on the kitchen stovetop. An occupant of the unit was located and brought out by firefighters to a waiting ambulance. They were then transported to a nearby hospital for smoke inhalation. A second ambulance was ordered to the scene to evaluate an additional occupant of the building, but that person was not transported. Authorities released no additional details.

Когда прибыли пожарные, им не сразу удалось попасть во двор - шлагбаум преградил путь. Как сообщают в местном тг-канале «Сводка Хабаровск» люди начали выламывать ограждение, чтобы помочь спасателям. «Надо убрать все шлагбаумы, блоки. Однако ограждение деблокировали, сотрудники МЧС немедленно приступили к эвакуации и уже тушили огонь. Им удалось вывести из подъезда 18 человек, в том числе трех детей. К счастью, пострадавших удалось избежать благодаря оперативным и слаженным действиям пожарных. Спустя полчаса после прибытия первых расчетов огонь удалось локализовать на площади 15 квадратных метров. Ein Bewohner wurde beim Versuch zu fliehen durch heiße Rauchgase verletzt und in ein Krankenhaus gebracht. Zwölf weitere Menschen konnten nur mithilfe sogenannter Fluchthauben in Sicherheit gebracht werden. Nach medizinischer Erstversorgung durch den Notarzt mussten drei von ihnen leicht verletzt ins Krankenhaus, neun konnten vor Ort verbleiben. Feuereinsatz in Köln: Zwölf Menschen mit Fluchthauben gerettet „Dank der schnellen und gezielten Löschmaßnahmen konnte eine Ausbreitung des Feuers auf weitere Gebäudeteile verhindert werden“, heißt es im Einsatzbericht.
